questions.question: How is standard deviation related to variance?
choices: It is the square of variance
It is the reciprocal of variance
It is the nonnegative square root of variance

questions.question: Which formula gives a z-score for value x, mean μ, and positive standard deviation σ?
What does a z-score of 0 mean?
What does a negative z-score indicate?
choices: The value lies below the mean
The original value must be negative
The value lies above the mean

questions.question: Can standard deviation be negative?
choices: Yes; when the mean is negative
Yes; when all values are below zero

questions.question: What units does standard deviation use?
choices: The same units as the original values
The reciprocal of the original units

questions.question: What units does a z-score have?
choices: Units of σ divided by units of x twice

questions.question: A value is 85, the mean is 70, and the standard deviation is 5. What is its z-score?
A value is 40, the mean is 50, and the standard deviation is 10. What is its z-score?
Why do z-scores help compare measurements on different scales?
choices: They make every original value identical
They express distances from means in standard-deviation units
They guarantee equal percentiles for differently shaped distributions

questions.question: If every data value increases by 7, what happens to standard deviation?
If every data value is multiplied by 3, what happens to standard deviation?
Why are deviations squared when calculating variance?
choices: Squaring prevents positive and negative deviations from canceling

questions.question: For a population consisting of 0 and 4, what is the population standard deviation?
Why does the usual sample variance use divisor n − 1 rather than n?
choices: It makes every sample variance smaller
It adjusts for estimating the population mean from the same sample
It removes one observed data value
It guarantees that the sample is random

questions.question: A score has z = 2, mean 60, and standard deviation 7. What is the original score?
A student earns 90 on a test with mean 80 and standard deviation 5, and 80 on another with mean 70 and standard deviation 10. Which performance is farther above its test mean in standardized units?
Two data sets have the same mean. One has standard deviation 2 and the other 8. Which is typically more spread out?
choices: The set with fewer decimal values

questions.question: A value is two standard deviations below a mean of 25 with standard deviation 3. What is the value?
Why is a z-score undefined when standard deviation equals zero?
choices: Its formula would require division by zero
The data must contain an outlier
